result.title: Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals
result.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) enables effective capability transfer between language models, yet the mechanisms underlying its failures are not fully understood. Across code generation and mathematical reasoning, OPD with larger-scale teachers exhibits early loss plateaus, with an average final loss reduction of 25.1% after 200 updates, compared with 96.2% for self-RL teachers, obtained by further reinforcement learning (RL) training of the initial student. To understand this difference, we analyze OPD as an idealized continuous-time dynamical system in the small-learning-rate limit. Our training-log diagnostics associate these plateaus with an early decline in a gradient-based learning-signal proxy while substantial loss remains; these measurements do not establish why the underlying gradient weakens. We further prove a local recovery guarantee for teachers sufficiently close to the initial student in a shared parameterization under regularity conditions, offering a conditional explanation for the success of self-RL teachers in our experiments. Across runs with and without loss plateaus, we observe small relative parameter changes (0.025-0.098%) and high similarity between the student's representations before and after OPD (linear CKA $>0.98$ across layers). These observations suggest that limited representation adaptation may contribute to learning-signal collapse, a hypothesis that remains to be tested. Code is available at https://github.com/leizhao7/opd-learning-signals.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 on-policy distillation 在代码生成与数学推理上为何出现损失平台期，将 OPD 视为小学习率下的连续时间动力学系统，用梯度型「学习信号」代理与逐层 CKA 表示相似度诊断学习信号衰减，并给出教师接近初始学生时的局部恢复性保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 属纯文本蒸馏训练分析，不直接涉及视觉或多模态推理；但其学习信号代理与逐层 CKA 表示漂移度量可能可供核查 LVR 训练中监督信号衰减、贡献分配以及 latent 表示相似度（层级、深度）的测量方式。
